codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured provider abstraction. BaseProvider ABC correctly defines abstract methods (translate, query, check). OllamaProvider extracts all existing Ollama logic faithfully. Factory function get_provider() dispatches correctly. Module-level wrappers preserve backward compatibility with identical behavior to pre-refactor code. 23 tests cover all 12 validation assertions. Only 2 files changed (engine.py, test_provider.py). No off-limits files modified. All 101 tests pass, ruff clean.

issues.description: test_base_provider_is_abstract and test_get_provider_unknown_raises use try/except pattern instead of idiomatic pytest.raises(). Functional but not idiomatic pytest style. Example: should use `with pytest.raises(TypeError): BaseProvider()`.

VAL-PROV-005 error tests (test_translate_connect_error_returns_none, test_translate_404_returns_none, etc.) verify return value is None but do not assert that appropriate error messages were printed to stderr. The implementation does print guidance messages to stderr for ConnectError and 404, but this is untested. Consider adding capsys/capfd assertions.

No explicit delegation test for module-level query_llm() wrapper. translate() and check_ollama() have delegation tests (test_module_translate_delegates_to_provider, test_module_check_ollama_delegates), but query_llm is only tested for importability/callability. A test like test_module_query_llm_delegates would strengthen VAL-PROV-009 coverage.

Module-level wrappers create a new OllamaProvider instance on every call via get_provider(). This is consistent with the pre-refactor behavior (VoxConfig() was created each call) and preserves backward compatibility, but is a micro-inefficiency for repeated calls. Not a bug — just a future optimization opportunity if caching becomes relevant.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker used try/except pattern for exception testing in pytest tests instead of pytest.raises(). AGENTS.md says 'Use unittest.mock.patch for mocking' but doesn't specify exception testing idiom. Could add a convention note about preferring pytest.raises() for exception assertions.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: tests/test_provider.py:33 — try: BaseProvider(); assert False except TypeError: pass — vs idiomatic: with pytest.raises(TypeError): BaseProvider()
